instruction: Count the words in the main essay body (excluding title, subtitle, references, and word count note) and add this count in parentheses at the end of the essay title.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires counting words in the main body and adding the count to the title. The main body has approximately 1087 words. Evaluator checks if the title contains a number in the range 1080-1095.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks that the number is in parentheses at the end of the title using regex pattern r'\((\d+)\)\s*$' (line 38)
Evaluator performs actual word counting of the essay body (lines 58-92), not just checking for any number in range

All required exclusions are properly implemented: title paragraph (line 65-66), subtitle heuristic (line 82-83), references section (lines 73-79), word count notes (lines 85-87), and empty paragraphs (lines 69-70)
Logic validates both format correctness (parentheses at end) AND semantic correctness (actual count matches with ±15 word tolerance)
Partial credit logic is sound: returns 1.0 for correct count, 0.7 for correct format but slightly off count, 0.0 for missing/incorrect format
Postconfig appropriately saves the file (Ctrl+S) before extraction, ensuring fresh state
Expected range [1080-1095] is semantically correct based on metadata calculation of ~1087 words
Edge cases are handled: empty paragraphs, missing content, exceptions (try-except block)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The subtitle detection heuristic (line 82-83: paragraph after title with <10 words) might not catch all subtitle formats. Could enhance by also checking paragraph styling/formatting, but current heuristic is reasonable given DOCX parsing limitations.
